newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran commerce minister designate urges new rules.
newsitem.headline: Iran commerce minister designate urges new rules.

text.p: Iran's commerce minister designate Mohammad Shariatmadari has said Tehran needs to adopt new and stable rules to develop its non-oil exports, particularly petrochemicals.

"New and more effective regulations are needed to pave the way for expansion of non-oil exports, boosting it to about half of Iran's total exports in the next four years," the official news agency IRNA quoted the minister designate as saying.
Currently non-oil products account for only about 15 percent of total exports in the world's third biggest oil exporting nation behind Saudi Arabia and Norway.
Shariatmadari said ever-changing regulations governing exports were one of the main difficulties facing Iran's export industries.

Since tough foreign exchange rules for exporters of Iran's main non-oil export -- carpets -- were relaxed in February, rug exports have risen sharply. This has lifted non-oil exports by about 30 percent since then.
"Iran's share of international trade now stands at a mere 0.34 percent, a figure not befitting a big country such as Iran," Shariatmadari said.

"Iran must aim to allocate the biggest chunk of its petrodollars to development of its petrochemical industries which currently brings the country some $650 million annually, matching the revenue from the 100-year-old carpet industry."
On Tuesday Iran's Majlis will start debating Shariatmadari's nomination, and those of the other 21 proposed ministers in President Mohammad Khatami's cabinet.
